newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Eurogold mine to begin production in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Eurogold mine to begin production in 1997.

text.p: Eurogold Madencilik, the Turkish subsidiary of Australia's Normandy Mining and Posgold, said on Monday it would begin producing gold this year at a mine in western Turkey after years of legal battles.
"We will begin production at the gold in November," Jack Testard, general manager of the company, was quoted as saying by the state-controlled Anatolian news agency.

Turkey's Council of State rejected two weeks ago an appeal by local residents and environmentalists to stop production at the mine, located at Ovacik village near the ancient city of Pergamum, because its method of production involved use of cyanide-leaching that could damage the nature.
Testard said the company would employ 240 people, 10 percent of the workforce coming from local people.

He said the company, set up in 1989, would process reserves at the site for about five years. "We will asses the reserves again after five years and may work there for another two or three years," he said.
He said all measures, including treatment systems, to protect the environment and health of people living nearby were taken, considering possibility of and earthquake in the area.
The company was severely criticised when it felled about 2,300 trees at the mine site earlier this year.
"We will plant three times as many trees that we cut. The trees we cut were of very low quality," Testard said.
Eurogold secured approval from the Turkish Environmental Ministry in March after its application six years ago.
Approval came after a team of mining experts reported the cyanide-leaching method would not harm public health or environment.
Reserves are estimated at 1.38 million tonnes at 11.7 grammes per tonne, with an identified mineral resource of 2.98 million tonnes at nine grammes per tonne, totalling 860,000 ounces.
Gold production is expected to be at an initial rate of 110,000 ounces a year at an operating cost below $150 per ounce.
